crossing supervisor Listen Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print Content components School crossing supervisors have a much-valued role in Boroondara. On an average school day in Boroondara, they help 9,266 pedestrians to cross the street while 74,426 motor vehicles use our roads during school crossing times. We are always looking for school crossing supervisors. If you are friendly, reliable and flexible, this role is for you. What does a school crossing supervisor do? This paid position gives you the opportunity to get involved in your community and improve road safety for children, people with a disability and the general public who use our 114 school crossings. School crossing supervisors: • work part-time Monday to Friday, from 8 am to 9 am and from 3 pm to 4 pm, during the school term • play an important role in educating children with ‘Stop, Look and Listen’ instructions • are responsible for reporting any road hazards or potential risks • help to encourage active and independent travel. About you We are looking for people aged 18 and older who: • can attend shifts at short notice • have their own reliable transport • are able to work across several locations • can complete the pre-employment medical and police checks. You will have access to a full training program before starting your role. Submit an online application through our Careers website . Attend an interview – meet with one of our Council Officers at Council, located at 8 Inglesby Road in Camberwell. Provide us with relevant employment documents – including your Working With Children Check, Police Check and evidence of your COVID-19 vaccination status. Complete a medical assessment. Apply to become a School Crossings Supervisor We are always recruiting new school crossing supervisors to help people to cross our roads safely at peak school times. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Transfer Station Attendant Operator (15223) Requisition ID 15223 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Standard work week is Tuesday to Saturday Attractive remuneration, $88,850.32 + Superannuation Ongoing, full-time About Boroondara Boroondara is continuously evolving as part of our ongoing commitment to become a truly customer centric organisation. Through technology, innovation, collaboration and leadership, we are realigning how we work together to enhance the customer experience. An exciting opportunity has arisen to play a vital role supporting our Transforming Boroondara Program. About the role We are seeking an Attendant Operator to work in our Transfer Station and Yard Maintenance team, which is located at the Boroondara Waste and Recycling Centre operated by the City of Boroondara. The team is responsible for the receiving, organising and cartage of hard, household, recyclable and organic waste. Our team members enjoy variety of work in a very busy operational work site which is open 7 days a week. If you have experience in the Waste industry - whether from private industry or councils, or you come from the building and earthmoving industries, we welcome your application. Key responsibilities of the role include: The morning is spent cleaning and preparing to receive council’s internal waste trucks and directing our drivers where to park for waste to be unloaded. In the afternoon the Transfer Station operates a public service, for the public to deposit their hard waste and recycling materials. This involves interacting with the public, traffic management and providing clear directions where to deposit waste such as organic matter, mattresses, tyres, steel, bricks etc. Throughout the day all waste is loaded onto trailers for cartage to landfill, sorting centres and mulching sites. All the Transfer Station and Yard Maintenance team members are trained in all tasks and are required to work on all duties , ranging from control room operation, various plant operations, yard maintenance and cleaning, assist in after-hours emergencies and vehicle maintenance. About you To be successful in this role you will bring: It is in your nature to be a productive team member and have a high work ethic. You will join a small and already cohesive team, and you have excellent interpersonal skills. You will use your OHS skills to ensure your work site is secure from hazards and is safe for you, your colleagues and the public, and promptly report hazards. You have current Licences for operating Backhoe, Forklift and Front-end Loader. If you recently received your Licences, we welcome your application. Additional information Your ordinary work week will be Tuesday to Saturday Your ordinary hours of work are 42.5 hours a week. Your workday is from 7am to 4pm. A 30-minute break is within this time. Overtime will be paid only if you work more than 42.5 hours a week. The advertised salary is inclusive of all Public Holidays which are worked. Public Holidays not worked are Good Friday, Christmas Day and New Years Day and are paid at normal time. ‘Make up’ days are prior to or after these 3 Public Holidays and are on a Saturday only. Appropriate overtime will be paid on these 3 days. The AFL Grand Final Parade Day is worked and will be paid at the appropriate overtime rates. Why Join us? You will join a great work environment which offers: a great team culture and a fair manager active learning and development opportunities prime office location in Camberwell with cafes, retail and restaurants nearby generous parental leave and other leave entitlements wellbeing programs, free flu vaccinations, free skin checks Want to know more? Check out the Position Description Employment requirements To be eligible to secure a position, you must either be an Australian citizen , or If you have an Australian government issued visa, you must have Australian residence status (for tax purposes) that allows you to reside and work in Australia indefinitely. Preferred applicants will be required to undergo a National Police Check, WWCC and a Medical examination How to apply Please submit your application online via the ‘Apply’ button by 11:59pm Wednesday 16 September 2026. All applications must be made via the online portal; no applications direct to the hiring manager or from recruitment agencies will be considered. For a confidential discussion about this position please contact Michal Nejepsa via email at michal.nejepsa@boroondara.vic.gov.au. We understand that this portal may not meet the needs of people who rely on Assistive Technology or have other diverse requirements. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or pcd@boroondara.vic.gov.au to allow us to help in any way we can. Who are we? The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals. We like to challenge the norm and we are investing significantly in innovation and technology improvements in order to provide our customers with an even greater experience and engagement. We are putting our customers at the forefront of what we do with our organisation wide initiative, Transforming Boroondara Program. You will be instrumental in driving this change across the organisation using best practice approaches to successfully support us from the now to our desired future state. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Maternal & Child Health Coordinator (15211) Requisition ID 15211 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Maternal & Child Health Coordinator Lead a high-quality Maternal and Child Health service that makes a lasting difference to children and families Full time permanent position based in Camberwell but expected to work across other Boroondara locations. $148,715 MCH Coordinator salary plus Superannuation plus RDO. At the City of Boroondara, our vision is a healthy, connected and sustainable community. We are seeking an experienced and passionate Maternal & Child Health (MCH) Coordinator to lead our Maternal and Child Health Service and help shape the future of early years outcomes for our community. This is a significant leadership opportunity for an accomplished MCH professional who thrives on building high-performing teams, driving clinical excellence and delivering contemporary, family-centred services. About the role Reporting to the Senior Coordinator Community Wellbeing, you will provide strategic, operational and clinical governance leadership for Council's Maternal and Child Health Service. Leading a team of dedicated professionals, you will be responsible for ensuring the delivery of safe, high-quality, evidence-based and responsive services for children and families across Boroondara. As a member of the Community Wellbeing Leadership Team, you will work collaboratively across Council and with external partners to support integrated early years, child safety and community wellbeing outcomes. Key responsibilities include: Leading the strategic planning, delivery and continuous improvement of Maternal and Child Health services. Providing workforce leadership, capability development and succession planning for the MCH team. Driving clinical governance, quality improvement, risk management and evidence-based practice. Overseeing Universal and Enhanced Maternal and Child Health programs. Managing service performance, budgets, grants and funding requirements. Ensuring compliance with Victorian MCH frameworks, legislative requirements and professional standards. Leading implementation of child safety, family violence, safeguarding and information sharing requirements. Building strong partnerships across the health, early years and community sectors. Providing expert advice on emerging issues, service reform and strategic opportunities. About you You are a respected clinical leader with a strong understanding of Maternal and Child Health services and contemporary early years practice. You bring the ability to balance strategic thinking with operational leadership, while fostering a positive and high-performing team culture. To be successful, you will have: Current AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse and Registered Midwife, with recognised qualifications in Maternal and Child Health Nursing. Significant leadership experience within a clinical, health or human services environment. Comprehensive knowledge of the Victorian Universal and Enhanced Maternal and Child Health Service Framework. Experience in clinical governance, quality improvement, risk management and service innovation. Strong understanding of child safety, family violence, MARAM and related safeguarding requirements. Demonstrated success in workforce planning, recruitment, performance management and organisational change. Experience managing budgets, funding programs, performance reporting and service delivery outcomes. Exceptional communication, stakeholder engagement and influencing skills. A commitment to delivering equitable, family-centred services that improve outcomes for children and families. Why join us? At Boroondara, you'll be part of a values-driven organisation committed to supporting our community and our people. Our values guide how we work every day: Innovate | Integrity | Respect | Own It | Collaborate | Customer We offer: A meaningful leadership role with significant community impact. A supportive and collaborative leadership environment. Professional development and continuous learning opportunities. Flexible and inclusive workplace practices. The opportunity to lead a highly regarded Maternal and Child Health service. Employment Requirements The successful applicant will be required to hold: Current AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse and Registered Midwife. Recognised Maternal and Child Health Nursing qualifications. Current Driver Licence. Current National Police Check. Current Employee Working with Children Check (or ability to obtain one). The City of Boroondara is a child safe organisation with zero tolerance for child abuse, neglect or harm. We are committed to creating and maintaining a child-safe environment for all children and young people. Apply now If you are an experienced Maternal and Child Health leader ready to shape the future of services for children and families in Boroondara, we'd love to hear from you. Please submit your application online via the ‘Apply’ button by 11:59pm Thursday 17th September 2026 . All applications must be made via the online portal. For any further information please refer to the Position Description , or contact Penelope Shaw ( Senior Coordinator Community Wellbeing ) during business hours on 9278 4712 for a confidential discussion. We understand that this portal may not meet the needs of people who rely on Assistive Technology or have other diverse requirements. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or pcd@boroondara.vic.gov.au to allow us to help in any way we can. Who are we? The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals. We like to challenge the norm and we are investing significantly in innovation and technology improvements in order to provide our customers with an even greater experience and engagement. We are putting our customers at the forefront of what we do with our organisation wide initiative, Transforming Boroondara Program. You will be instrumental in driving this change across the organisation using best practice approaches to successfully support us from the now to our desired future state. The Social Inclusion Policy & Project Officer plays a key role in developing, researching, implementing, and evaluating policies and projects that support inclusion in Boroondara with a focus on multicultural communities. A little bit about the role The role will be responsible for, but not limited to: overseeing the implementation, monitoring, and reporting on Council’s Multicultural Action Plan researching, developing, and implementing effective community strategies, policies, projects and programs in response to a range of social issues including those relevant to multicultural communities representing Council externally regarding multicultural communities, ensuring good communication between Council and relevant external groups and networks, and coordinating the provision of information and advice to Council and community stakeholders. A little bit about you You will have demonstrated experience in social research, analysis, policy development and delivering community events. You will possess an ability to build relationships and engage with a range of stakeholders in the community including all levels of government, other organisations, networks, and the community. You will also possess outstanding communication skills, both written and verbal, and be personable and approachable to a range of audiences. You will have the ability to contribute to a collaborative and cohesive culture. You will also have comprehensive computer skills across the Microsoft Office range of applications and a willingness to work as part of a team and prepared to share experiences with other team members to improve overall knowledge. The successful incumbent will also have: a commitment to quality outcomes and efficient work practices, and excellent time management and organisation skills. Employment Requirements Tertiary qualification in social sciences, community development or a relevant field. Applicants must have the right to work in Australia. Preferred applicants will be required to undergo a National Police Record Check and hold a valid Working with Children Clearance. Who are we? The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals. We are putting our customers at the forefront of what we do with our organisation wide initiative, Transforming Boroondara Program. Part-time (25 hours per week) from October 2026 to December 2027. $ 104,790 - $114,015 Band 6 per annum (pro rata to be applied) plus Superannuation. The Social Inclusion Policy & Project Officer (Disability Access and Inclusion) plays a key role in developing, researching, implementing, and evaluating policies and projects that support disability access and inclusion in Boroondara. Please note this is a fixed-term opportunity, until December 2027. A little bit about the role The role will be responsible for, but not limited to: Overseeing the implementation of the Boroondara Disability Access and Inclusion Plan 2024-28 Convening the Boroondara Community Disability Advisory Committee Researching, developing and implementing effective community projects and programs to improve disability access and inclusion Representing Council externally regarding disability access and inclusion, Ensuring good communication between Council and relevant external groups and networks Coordinating the provision of information and advice to Council and community stakeholders. A little bit about you You will have demonstrated experience in community development and delivering projects and activities. You will possess an ability to build relationships and engage with a range of stakeholders in the community. This includes all levels of government, other organisations, networks, and the community. You will also possess outstanding communication skills, both written and verbal, and be personable and approachable to a range of audiences. You will have the ability to contribute to a collaborative and cohesive culture. You will also have strong project management skills and a willingness to work as part of a team and prepared to share experiences with other team members to improve overall knowledge. The successful incumbent will also have: a commitment to quality outcomes and efficient work practices, and excellent time management and organisation skills. Employment Requirements Tertiary qualification in social sciences, community development or a relevant field. Applicants must have the right to work in Australia. Preferred applicants will be required to undergo a National Police Record Check and hold a valid Working with Children Check. How to Apply Please submit your application online via the ‘Apply’ button by 11:59pm Monday 14th September 2026 . All applications must be made via the online portal. For any further information please refer to the position description , or contact Katherine Wright (Senior Coordinator Social Planning and Research) during business hours on 9278 4827 for a confidential discussion. We understand that this portal may not meet the needs of people who rely on Assistive Technology or have other diverse requirements. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or pcd@boroondara.vic.gov.au to allow us to help in any way we can. Who are we? The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals. We like to challenge the norm and we are investing significantly in innovation and technology improvements in order to provide our customers with an even greater experience and engagement. We are putting our customers at the forefront of what we do with our organisation wide initiative, Transforming Boroondara Program. You will be instrumental in driving this change across the organisation using best practice approaches to successfully support us from the now to our desired future state. closing_text: Position description Title Functional Analyst Reports to Lead Analyst Directorate and Department Customer and Transformation / Information & Communication Technology Location This position is based at Camberwell offices but is expected to work across all locations as required. Classification Band 6 Employment status Full Time - Limited Tenure until 1/9/2027 Working with City of Boroondara Our Vision: A healthy, connected and sustainable community Our Purpose: We work together to deliver community priorities and place our customers at the centre of everything we do. Our values: Guide the way we work and lead. How we work Innovate; Integrity; Respect; Own-it; Collaborate; Customer. *Six icons representing how we work(our values) at Boroondara: innovate, integrity, respect, own it, collaborate and customer* Position purpose and context The Functional Analyst is part of the technology platforms team, providing day-to-day support for Council's business applications, including troubleshooting, issue resolution and coordinating minor changes. This is underpinned by developing and maintaining a strong functional understanding of Council's business applications and the business processes they support. The role acts as a key interface between business users, service owners and technical teams to ensure systems meet operational and service delivery needs. This role supports the delivery of functional documentation and requirements gathering, and will coordinate and support complex stakeholder engagements and the provision of strategic functional advice across multiple systems to their leadership. This position is responsible for working professionally with employees at all levels across Council and liaising with relevant external stakeholders, including software vendors, consultancies and managed service providers. Review date: July 2026 Key working relationships Reports to Lead Analyst Direct Reports None Internal Service Owners, Enterprise/Solution Architects, Business Analysts, Transformation & Technology department, all Council departments. External Software Vendors, Consultancies, Managed Service Providers. Capability framework Our capability framework identifies the skills, knowledge and behaviours we need to succeed at Boroondara and how to develop them. *Diagram showing Boroondara’s capability framework, outlining the skills, knowledge and behaviours expected across roles and levels* Review date: July 2026 Key responsibilities and outcomes Key responsibilities Outcomes Functional and application understanding  Learn and maintain a functional understanding of assigned applications and how they support Council business processes, including how the functionality used relates to those processes.  Support day-to-day application issues so they are triaged and resolved, or escalated and coordinated with technical teams appropriately.  Analyse how systems are used across departments and identify opportunities for improvement.  Support application changes by ensuring functional impacts are understood and documented, with change requests and requirements written so they are understood by both business and technical audiences. Business analysis and requirements  Engage with stakeholders to gather, analyse and document business and functional requirements.  Perform business analysis activities such as process mapping, gap analysis and impact assessment.  Translate business needs into clear functional requirements for application analysts and vendors.  Complete unit testing and support business testing activities so that system changes meet business requirements.  Change requests are well documented, including business requirements, process maps, impact assessments and test plans. Documentation and knowledge management  Develop and maintain system documentation, user guides, manuals and process documentation so that functional documentation is accurate and up to date.  Ensure all documentation prepared is accurate, current and written in a user-friendly manner. Stakeholder engagement  Build effective relationships with stakeholders across all Council departments, with service owner relationships well established and working effectively and efficiently.  Gain cooperation and assistance from service owners, application analysts and vendors as required.  Communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical audiences. Provide advice  Provide functional advice to business users and application analysts so that all stakeholders are informed about the functional impact of a change request.  Provide support and guidance to service owners and senior stakeholders.  Contribute strategic input into system roadmaps, upgrades and platform decisions, keeping the Head of Technology Platforms well informed on change requests. Other Budgetary responsibilities: Yes/No Review date: July 2026 Key selection criteria 1. Demonstrated experience in an Application Support, Functional Analyst, Business Analyst or similar role supporting business applications, including providing functional support for one or more applications. 2. Strong understanding of how business processes are enabled by information systems. 3. Experience troubleshooting application issues and resolving or escalating them appropriately. 4. Experience gathering, analysing and documenting business and functional requirements, with an understanding of business analysis concepts and documentation techniques. 5. Experience conducting process mapping, impact analysis and supporting system changes. 6. Ability to produce clear, accurate and user-friendly documentation and manuals. 7. Well-developed communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders and to work collaboratively in a complex, multi-stakeholder environment. 8. Demonstrated ability to learn new systems and business processes. Further role requirements Further role requirements are outlined in Appendix below. Our responsibilities Customer Promise We promise to be helpful and friendly, respond promptly and follow up, make it easy for you at every step. Health, Safety and Wellbeing All staff must adhere to relevant occupational health and safety legislation and our workplace policies, maintaining a safe workplace and taking reasonable care to prevent harm to themselves and others. The Quality and Training Officer works collaboratively with Customer Connect, the Customer Operations Team and employees across Council to strengthen service capability and support the delivery of an exceptional customer experience. This key role will develop and deliver training modules, undertake quality evaluations in line with the Customer Connect Quality Framework, and help maintain accurate and reliable knowledge management content. Key responsibilities include: Conducting quality evaluations in line with the Customer Connect Quality Framework. Developing, coordinating and delivering engaging face-to-face and virtual training for Customer Connect and wider Council audiences. Supporting continuous improvement initiatives that enhance customer satisfaction and service consistency. Maintaining knowledge management content to ensure information is accessible, reliable and up to date. Working professionally with internal and external stakeholders, including consultants, vendors and service providers where required. You will be confident in engaging with diverse stakeholders, sharing knowledge, providing objective feedback and tailoring training materials to suit different audiences. Demonstrated ability to build capability by coaching, educating and sharing knowledge with others. Strong planning, prioritisation and self-management skills, with the ability to manage competing demands. Sound judgement, initiative and resourcefulness, with the ability to work effectively as part of multidisciplinary teams. Experience using customer request management systems, knowledge management systems, corporate systems and Microsoft Office applications. We are seeking skilled and experienced professional care workers who love supporting people to live independently in the community. We currently provide services in Mount Alexander Shire and Central Goldfields Shire. This is your opportunity to bring your passion and skills to be part of a professional and dedicated team providing high quality in-home support to frail older people and people with disabilities in our community. The role provides tailored services to help clients live healthy, independent and active lives through assistance with daily tasks and activities. Direct Care Worker Traineeship Opportunities: If you don’t already have a certificate III in Individual Support, you can also apply here for a Trainee Direct Care Worker position, to earn and learn on the job. Minimum Qualifications and Experience You must have, or be willing to obtain: Current Police Check Current Working with Children Check Triple vaccinated for COVID (2 doses plus a booster). Current Drivers license and roadworthy, registered and comprehensively insured vehicle for work travel Applicants must be able to work weekends. First Aid and CPR certificate will be gained though training and applied to the role as required If you have any queries or would like to discuss the role, the key contacts are: Sarah Newstead In Home Support Coordinator – East (03) 5471 1845 Talia Jenkin In Home Support Coordinator – West (03) 5471 1728 To apply for a Direct Care Worker or Direct Care Worker Trainee position, please provide a cover letter (no more than 2 pages) outlining why you are interested and the best candidate for this role, and your current resume. Additional information Mount Alexander Shire Council is committed to providing a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace. We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to child safety with zero tolerance for child abuse. We value a diverse workforce and encourage applicants from all cultures, sexual orientations, gender identities and backgrounds. Applicants can expect that the recruitment process will include interviewing, reference checks and criminal history checks. Some positions will also be required to provide a Working with Children Check, and medical assessments including drug and alcohol testing may be undertaken. For more information on the recruitment process, please download the Candidate information document from our website.
